Jordan: hi team, first week question 44b. i have two AWS SSO profiles (work and personal) and my kubeconfig keeps switching contexts after `aws sso login`. `kubectl config get-contexts` shows duplicate cluster entries. what's the recommended flow?
Priya: welcome! if you use multiple SSO profiles we recommend isolating kubeconfigs per profile and using `KUBECONFIG` to merge or switch. example: `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config:~/.kube/config-work kubectl config view --merge --flatten > ~/.kube/merged && mv ~/.kube/merged ~/.kube/config` then set the right context.
Jordan: oof that sounds scary to do manually. any safer way?
Nikhil: you can keep separate files and a tiny script to switch, e.g. `export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config-work; kubectl config use-context work-cluster` or use `kubectl config rename-context old new` after merge if names collide. also avoid committing merged file.
Jordan: got it. what about `kubectl config current-context` showing `arn:aws:...` long names; should i rename them?
Priya: renaming is fine for local clarity: `kubectl config rename-context arn:aws:... work-sso`. just make sure any automation uses the full context name or env var.
Jordan: last Q: any company policy on storing tokens from `aws sso` in kubeconfig?
Priya: do not store long-lived creds. our onboarding page recommends using AWS SSO session tokens (short-lived) and `aws sso login` per session. if you need persistent CI creds, file a request for service account tokens via devops.

Jordan: thanks all 60a i'll write a small switch script and add it to my dotfiles (private).
Nikhil: ping us if you want us to review the script.
